Enrolled in a clinical trial for a novel cholesterol-lowering agent, Drug X.
The trial consists of 300 patients with elevated LDL cholesterol who are randomized to receive either Drug X or placebo.
Over a 6-month period, researchers collect data on LDL reduction and monitor for adverse events.
The primary outcome is a statistically significant reduction in LDL cholesterol compared to placebo.
No long-term cardiovascular outcomes are measured, and the sample size is insufficient to detect rare adverse effects.
The investigators report a significant mean LDL reduction in the Drug X group compared to placebo, with a p-value of 0.01.
The study is not blinded, but all participants are actual patients with the condition of interest.

The study enrolls 6,000 patients who are randomized to receive either Drug X or a statin and are followed for five years.
The primary endpoint is the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death.
The trial is double-blinded and powered to detect a 20% reduction in MACE with Drug X relative to the statin group.
After data analysis, the investigators report that the relative risk reduction for MACE with Drug X is statistically significant compared to the statin, with a p-value < 0.01.
The study protocol was submitted to the FDA as part of a new drug application.
